name: Miriam Achterberg-Osei
description: Formerly a licensed Vantablack director with three profitable neural-dramas to her name, Achterberg-Osei walked away from her contract in 2196 after the corp surgically altered her cut of a film without her knowledge before release. She has since operated entirely on pirate mesh networks, producing neural-feed shorts that circulate via dead drop and encrypted relay. Her underground work is structurally experimental — feeds that loop, contradict themselves, and leave emotional residue that viewers describe as 'productive damage.'
cultural_impact: Her underground reputation is so significant that several Tier 4 collectors pay premium rates for authenticated dead-drop chips of her work, creating a black market with its own authentication hierarchy.
story_hooks: She surfaces briefly to send a message to a journalist — she has completed a full-length neural feature and wants it released simultaneously on every pirate mesh node in M88, but needs help coordinating the drop.
The Vantablack edit of her stolen film is currently in wide release under a different director's name, and the real director is gathering witnesses to go public.
A young Vantablack director reaches out to her in secret, claiming to be in the same situation she was in 2196 and asking what to do.
